Viewed through the Financial Stability Report lens, the hold on the policy rate and the deceleration of Treasury redemptions are modestly supportive. However, the latest SLOOS points to still-tight credit conditions: banks report continued tightening of standards for C&I (across firm sizes) and CRE, higher minimum credit-score requirements for consumer loans, and expectations for higher delinquencies and charge-offs. Demand from firms remains soft, with banks citing the economic outlook, industry-specific issues, and lower risk tolerance. Combined with elevated FSR vulnerabilities (CRE stress, nonbank/private credit leverage, large MMF footprints/short-term funding linkages, and unrealized losses at banks) and lingering inflation risks, the balance of risks is more cautious than the macro “solid” growth language implies. Net tone: modestly positive but more muted given SLOOS-confirmed credit tightening.
